runtime Type.Void/Value.Void and function no_result already express this distinction.

not permission to admit CLI System.Void as an ordinary .NET generic argument.

## 2026-10-10 — Assessing the module divergence

- **Author:** “Is the approach with modules sound? Our diverging semantics”.
- **Assistant assessment:** the bounded assembly-owned, flat namespace-module model
  is coherent and useful for declaration discovery. Compared with .NET physical
  modules and open namespaces, it carries tooling and interoperability costs;
  no performance advantage is claimed.
- **Assistant qualification:** distinct assembly-qualified owners do not prohibit
  overlapping names across dependencies. Deterministic ambiguity handling and an
  explicit qualification/alias route are recommended follow-up design work, not
  newly adopted compiler policy. Ownership must not implicitly establish module
  privacy, independent loading or scheduling, or complete AOT metadata retention.
- **Action/outcome:** checked Microsoft's Module and C# namespace documentation and
  recorded the [soundness review](declaration-modules.md#soundness-review--2026-10-10).
  No implementation or roadmap reprioritization is part of this assessment; the
  native traversal and guest discovery work remains open. No subsequent author
  decision on these recommendations is recorded.

## 2026-10-11 — .NET 11 union JSON contract clarified

- **Author direction:** build a JSON serializer for union types matching .NET.
  In response to the assistant's clarification question, the author initially

  that premise: “I don't even think that .NET 11 unions use polymorphic discriminators?”

  specifies direct active-payload JSON without a wrapper or discriminator, default
  token-kind classification, and explicit classifiers for ambiguous shapes.
  This is the union compatibility target; the earlier discriminator answer is
  superseded by this clarification, not retained as a separate requirement.

  as a native library. A .NET 11 comparison consumer confirms number/string/default
  wire values and ambiguity/unknown-shape rejection. The neoCLR interpreter reaches
  the matching root assertions but fails when constructing a reflected union array.
  Native compilation rejects union arrays under its current reflection element
  profile; native value boxing also requires investigation. This is incomplete
  qualification, not a claim of native union serialization support. Automatic union
  metadata discovery, structural classifiers and nullable case selection remain open.
- **Representation difference under investigation:** Raven rejects supplying a known
  inactive default union in ordinary code. The prototype supplies an explicit empty
  case for JSON null; this must be documented as a gap from .NET 11 default-union
  semantics, not silently described as equivalent.

- **Integration request:** the author subsequently requested integration into main
  and removal of the worktree and branch. The validated JsonArray sequence change
  is integrated as runtime code; the unfinished converter changes are preserved as
  an [explicit experiment patch](experiments/json-converters/README.md), with their

## 2026-10-12 — MethodImpl and foreign imports

- **Author question:** “How does MethodImplAttribute fit into this model? I mean
  with do have internal calls etc also.”
- **Assistant explanation:** extern denotes a declaration without a source body.
  MethodImpl(InternalCall) selects a runtime-owned implementation identified by its
  runtime service contract; NativeImport selects an external library/export with an
  explicit ABI and marshalling descriptor. They are mutually exclusive implementation
  providers. MethodImpl also has .NET implementation options such as NoInlining; those
  are distinct from choosing a provider and must not imply unsupported neoCLR behavior.
- **Inspection:** neoCLR already separates impl_flags/InternalCall from native imports
  and rejects their combination. Current Raven runtime-service admission is deliberately
  narrow (internal extern namespace functions in neoCLR.Runtime). The latest imported
  symbol IsExtern fix recognizes NativeImport only; InternalCall readback remains a
  gap, not an intended semantic distinction.
- **Assistant proposal:** eventually expose implementation kind separately from
  implementation options and derive IsExtern for both native-import and internal-call
  declarations. No implementation or author acceptance of this proposal is claimed.
  [.NET MethodImplOptions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.compilerservices.methodimploptions)
  and [CoreCLR core-library boundaries](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/coreclr/botr/corelib.md)
  support the runtime-owned versus public foreign-import distinction.

## 2026-10-13 — HTTP execution phases and runtime concurrency

- **Author observation:** Other servers can advance different requests through
  asynchronous processing phases; neoCLR should consider HTTP-layer scheduling
  and runtime infrastructure as well as GC. This is a proposed architectural
  direction, not approval of a particular native parser or scheduling design.
- **Assistant assessment:** Agrees that I/O readiness, bounded parsing work,
  backpressure and inexpensive suspension/resumption are separate concerns from
  allocation. Yielding at every parsing step would add overhead; process available
  bytes in batches and suspend when waiting or when a fairness budget is exhausted.
  HTTP protocol state can remain in the library while generic I/O, scheduler and
  buffer-lifetime services belong in the runtime.
- **Current evidence:** HttpServer already composes asynchronous accept/receive/send,
  but receives in 256-byte blocks and uses explicit outcome adapters. The retained
  Raven benchmark awaits ServeOne serially and the common client has concurrency
  one, so the pilot does not measure cross-request interleaving. Interleaving alone
  cannot explain or remove its single-request latency gap. Existing profiles point
  to GC/root overhead but do not exclude HTTP control-flow/buffering costs.
- **Proposed next bounded work:** Keep the current baseline; add a separate concurrent
  workload with slow/fragmented peers, per-phase timing, scheduler/continuation and
  I/O operation counts. Use those measurements to evaluate bounded concurrent
  serving, larger batched reads and fairness/backpressure across managed/native
  execution modes. No new runtime API or implementation is introduced here.
- **Primary comparisons:** [.NET pipelines and backpressure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/io/pipelines),
  [Go connection goroutines](https://go.dev/pkg/net/http/?m=old), and
  [Node event-loop blocking](https://nodejs.org/en/learn/asynchronous-work/dont-block-the-event-loop).
  These differ in scheduling model; they do not imply every parser yields midway
  through each token or that parsing must live in a native runtime service.

### 2026-10-14 — Assessment of native composition direction

- Author asked whether the direction is sound and whether neoCLR should support
  unions and intersections. Assistant recommends continuing both as native type
  specifications with conservative, explicit rules. This is a recommendation,
  not a newly approved production contract or a formal soundness result.
- Rationale: preserve alternatives and combined trait requirements across assembly
  and generic boundaries. Scala provides established language precedents for
  [unions](https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/new-types/union-types.html)
  and [intersections](https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/new-types/intersection-types.html);
  [.NET generic constraints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/generics/constraints-on-type-parameters)
  already express conjunctions of interfaces, while the proposed compositions
  extend the available signature contracts. Language precedents alone do not
  establish the need for native runtime support; cross-language preservation is
  the intended benefit, with added loader, verifier, reflection and backend cost.
- Assistant cautions: overlapping union alternatives do not preserve a selected
  case (for example, substituting HttpError for T); use tagged unions when case
  identity matters. The author's sealed-bound restriction is a simplification
  policy, not a mathematical requirement, and does not alone exclude impossible
  intersections of unrelated classes. Intersection returns remain valid.
- Recommended next evidence: executable Task<Response<T> | HttpError | JsonError>
  paths, substitution/constraint rejection tests, and closure of representation
  gaps before stabilizing metadata/ABI. Existing bounded interpreter consumers
  demonstrate feasibility, not production completeness; value storage, nullability,
  member conflicts, variance, reflection and JIT/AOT still need specified coverage.
  [Current POC evidence](experiments/structural-compositions/README.md).

## 2026-10-15 — Structural type direction and language precedents

The author asked: “Is this direction with structural types still sound? Is there
any language that has done similar?” The assistant assessed the architecture as
coherent, while distinguishing that judgment from a formal type-safety proof or
completion of the runtime ABI. Structural composition of nominal types does not
require implicit interface conformance or duck typing.

Primary-source comparisons reviewed by the assistant:

- [Scala 3 unions](https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/new-types/union-types.html)
  and [intersections](https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/new-types/intersection-types.html)
  demonstrate anonymous composition of class/trait types, including generic
  intersection bounds. They are language-semantic precedents, not evidence for
  neoCLR's particular value-container representation or reflection contract.
- [Julia types](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/manual/types/#Type-Unions) combine
  nominal/parametric types with runtime union types. Its
  [isbits union optimization](https://docs.julialang.org/en/v1/devdocs/isbitsunionarrays/)
  demonstrates inline payload storage with type tags for eligible unions.
  Julia's dynamic type model and union types are not the same as neoCLR's proposed
  distinct union value containers; this does not select neoCLR's ABI.
- [TypeScript compatibility](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/type-compatibility)
  and [compositions](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/unions-and-intersections.html)
  provide an ergonomic comparison. Its structural object compatibility differs
  from neoCLR's explicitly implemented nominal interfaces.

The assistant recommended maintaining separate contracts for type identity,
assignability, payload/boxing identity and physical layout. Open generic
substitution, overlapping union alternatives, variance, reflection and GC/layout
remain validation obligations. The no-final-class intersection rule is a
conservative project restriction, not a mathematical necessity: a final class
already implementing an interface can have a meaningful, redundant intersection.
No change to that author-selected restriction was made or inferred.

## 2026-10-23 — Media type representation discussion

- **Author:** Asked how System.Web should represent media types in HTTP APIs,
  suggesting predefined media types and a value object retaining their structure.
- **Assistant proposal:** An immutable MediaType value object, provisionally in
  System.Web.Http, with type/subtype, optional structured suffix, read-only
  parameters, parsing/formatting and explicit equality semantics; a grouped
  MediaTypes catalog supplies typed values. Prefer an ordinary reference class
  with value equality, following HttpMethod, rather than a closed enum or special
  runtime representation. Keep Accept ranges and quality weights separate. Add
  typed content overloads and retain string migration paths; distinguish absent
  from malformed incoming Content-Type.
- **Comparison:** .NET 10 supplies string names through
  [MediaTypeNames](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.mime.mediatypenames?view=net-10.0)
  and mutable structured values through
  [MediaTypeHeaderValue](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.http.headers.mediatypeheadervalue?view=net-10.0).
  Typed immutable presets would deliberately differ, making sharing safe and
  avoiding caller-side parsing, at the cost of a different API and copy-on-change
  operations. ASP.NET Core's structured header API and Rust
  [mime 0.3.17](https://docs.rs/mime/0.3.17/mime/struct.Mime.html)
  provide additional decomposition precedents. Sources consulted 2026-10-23;
  [RFC 9110 sections 5.6.6, 8.3.1 and 12.5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html)
  govern parameter syntax, case rules and Accept ranges.
- **Open:** Naming/namespace, duplicate-parameter policy and precise equality
  require a contract before implementation. Differential .NET checks, quoted
  parameter round trips, case-sensitive boundaries, invalid inputs and an HTTP
  consumer are proposed validation, not performed tests. Independent .NET project
  and API-review issue research remain open. This is a design discussion, with no
  author acceptance, runtime implementation or roadmap reprioritization inferred.

- **Author acceptance and refinement:** Directed implementation and a commit, then
  requested tests and attention to allocation efficiency, caching and interning,
  comparing the intended convenience with HttpMethod. Clarified that structured
  values should materialize lazily: HTTP internals can retain validated primitive
  strings without constructing a MediaType for every header.
- **General author direction:** Value objects define consumer-facing contracts;
  internal processing should prefer validated primitives when a wrapper adds no
  value. The assistant recorded this in AGENTS.md and design-research.md, with
  consistent validation, bounded caches and measurement requirements. This does
  not replace structured public contracts with primitive-only APIs.
- **Assistant action:** Implements one shared admission scanner for raw HTTP and
  structured parsing, lazy cached content/message access, typed content overloads,
  cached preset values/strings/hashes, retained parameter views and focused tests.
  Allocation diagnostics identified string-to-Object conversions in the test's
  ReferenceEquals call; hot formatting is measured without those conversions.
  The catalog uses a namespace because native nested static classes are currently
  unsupported; no compiler change or Runtime Contract encoding is introduced.
- **Author follow-up:** After this slice, inspect Uri efficiency and perhaps Path.
  The assistant will measure and address a bounded opportunity after the media
  type commit; this is a follow-up task, not a permanent roadmap reprioritization.

- **Author clarification:** Cited prior HTTP server performance loss from storing

## 2026-10-23 — Plain-text throughput, worker efficiency and reference servers

The author asked to compare neoCLR's throughput with other web servers and to
investigate their language/runtime/API approaches: being the fastest is not required,
but the attainable result should be measured. The author then clarified that plain
request/response handling is the basic measurement, with complex samples secondary.
An initial emphasis on throughput with few allocations was subsequently refined:
“Primary is increasing throughout via the use of worker thread. And using the
least CPU as possible,” followed by the correction “Throughput.” Allocation counts
are therefore secondary diagnostics, not the first optimization gate; JSON comes
after the plain baseline.

The assistant created direct ten-byte response consumers for neoCLR, Go, Node and
Kestrel and researched .NET thread-pool/async guidance, Go connection goroutines,
Node event-loop/worker separation, and Hyper/Tokio async services and ownership.
The first Python driver saturated its CPU; a subsequent Go HTTP driver encountered
ephemeral-port exhaustion at higher connection-close rates. The assistant retained
those calibration outcomes and used a two-processor compiled TCP client that waits
for server EOF, without changing system TCP settings.

All 14 final comparison trials pass response checks and clean shutdown. neoCLR
measures 485–491 requests/s with one owner and 1,531–1,693 with four. Estimated
server CPU per response grows from about 2.05 ms to 2.28–2.42 ms; single-setting
reference servers achieve roughly 19,000–25,000 requests/s in this short local
connection-close workload. These are baseline observations, not production maxima
or framework rankings. Shared async HTTP, keep-alive, CPU attribution on the new
fixture and future throughput improvements remain open.

The earlier in-progress synchronous safepoint polling optimization was completed
and committed with GC stress tests and separate graph measurements. It is retained
as runtime evidence, not counted as a plain HTTP improvement.
See [primary baseline, sources and reproduction](../benchmarks/http-server/primitive-comparison/README.md).

continues the plaintext baseline investigation and discovers that its earlier

transport/OS/client delivery without establishing its cause or a GC performance win.
